question: Which of the following is an epigraphic record for the reign of King Harsha?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Muzaffarnagar Seals**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Muzaffarnagar Seals** are not considered an epigraphic record of King Harsha's reign.
 
• There is no known direct evidence linking these seals to King Harsha, who ruled during the **7th century CE**.
 
• King Harsha's reign is known through prominent inscriptions and records such as the **Banskhera Copper Plate** and the **Nalanda Seals**, but the Muzaffarnagar Seals do not belong to this list.
 
• Epigraphic records typically include inscriptions on **metal plates, stone, or seals** that provide historical details, but these seals lack definitive evidence connecting them to Harsha.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Banskhera Copper Plate**__

 __
 
• The **Banskhera Copper Plate** is one of the most significant records of King Harsha's reign.
 
• It provides details about Harsha’s administration, his titles, and his patronage of Buddhism.
 
• It is written in **Sanskrit** and inscribed on copper plates.
 
 
 
• **Nalanda Seals**__
 __
 
• The **Nalanda Seals** were found in the ancient **Nalanda University**, which Harsha patronized.
 
• These seals confirm Harsha’s donations to the university and his association with the spread of Buddhism.
 
• They provide evidence of the flourishing academic and cultural environment during his rule.
 
 
 
• **Aihole Inscription**__
 
 
• The **Aihole Inscription** is associated with the **Chalukyan King Pulakeshin II**, not King Harsha.
 
• It describes Pulakeshin’s victory over Harsha in the **battle of Narmada**.
 
• This inscription is a critical source for understanding the political landscape of early medieval India.
